profile.title: Profile
profile.summary: Developer with a physics-and-math brain, working with LLMs and image generation since 2020, after years of smaller neural networks. I **don’t buy or sell buzzwords**, I know **what models can and cannot do**, and I turn vague ideas into working prototypes — or clean up the ones that got vibe-coded into a corner.
profile.paragraph1: Developer with a physics-and-math brain and a knack for building practical tools that turn AI buzz into actual features. Ever since 2020, most of my work revolves around LLMs and image generation, following years of messing with smaller neural networks. This means I **don't buy or sell buzzwords**, I understand things **a level or two deeper than most**, and I've developed an **intuition for what models can and cannot do**.
profile.paragraph2: I've built systems from scratch, simplified convoluted integrations, and turned vague ideas into working prototypes — across open-source, startups, and global advertising giants.

items.text: the architecture, the staged pipeline and the pre-push gate that let a crowd of agents ship without drifting — set up on your codebase, then handed over as checked-in procedure rather than as advice. It has been handed over once already, and the engineers who took it carried it to projects of their own.

items.label: Rescue and diagnosis
items.text: the prototype that got vibe-coded into a corner, and the agent that doesn't do what you expected — usually the same purchase.

items.label: Standing technical judgment
items.text: build-vs-buy calls, and a straight answer on what the models still cannot do.

engineeringSystem.title: The Engineering System
items: Feature-sliced architecture held by linters, so a crowd of agents working at once cannot drift the structure.
A staged pipeline — plan, implement, review, finalize — each stage its own session, with reviewable artifacts between them.
Branch hygiene held in-session: a gate of concurrent checks before every push, the production build among them, so no agent contaminates main with code that breaks it.
CI/CD that fits your workflow — ship every commit off main, staging-based release cycles, or release trains.

workingStyle.title: Working Style
paragraphs: I'm the kind of developer you can generally leave unattended, as long as the overall vector is clear. I have enough life expertise to figure stuff on my own, enough imagination to fill the missing pieces, and a "treat any job as if it was your own brainchild" mentality.
In other words: a surprisingly low-maintenance LLM tinkerer with a soft spot for TypeScript, ready to prototype, debug, or sanity-check your AI-infused ambitions.

handsOnLead.title: Working Style
paragraphs: Hands-on is the point: I set the direction and write the rules the work runs on, then stay in the code — reviewing what the agents ship, fixing what the gate catches, and deciding what gets built next. Give me the vector and I'll own the result as if the company were my own.
Handing over is part of the job rather than the end of it: the procedure lives in the repository, where the next engineer will find it, and at Playgram I mentored two developers along the way.

aiExpertise.title: AI Expertise
paragraphs: I tend to stick to a more "economical" paradigm of AI usage: smaller prompts, a close eye on context limits, and no hoping that a model fed everything will sort it out on its own. My expertise predates the ChatGPT hype cycle, which means I understand not just the APIs, but the patterns and limitations underneath them — which is where most of the hard problems live.

header.tagline: Fractional, hands-on CTO for AI-native delivery

profile.summary: 158 days, **250,000 lines of production TypeScript** with none of it hand-written, **up to 20 agents at once** and **a deploy every 2.4 days** — on a live product that never left production. I lead AI-native delivery hands-on: the agents, the pipeline they ship through, and the handover to the engineers who carry the platform on.
profile.paragraph1: 158 days, **250,000 lines of production TypeScript**, none of it hand-written, up to **20 agents working at once**, and **a production deploy every 2.4 days** — on a live product that stayed in production for its users the whole way through. The engineering platform I built to get there outlived my involvement: three engineers run it today, and it travels to their new projects as a checked-in boilerplate.
profile.paragraph2: Most of my work has revolved around LLMs and image generation ever since 2020, following years of messing with smaller neural networks. This means I **don't buy or sell buzzwords**, I understand things **a level or two deeper than most**, and I've developed an **intuition for what models can and cannot do**. What I lead is the delivery — the agents, the pipeline they ship through, and the handover to the engineers who carry the platform on — at founder-and-small-team scale, through the work rather than the org chart.

intro.quote: “AI as collaborator, not tool or replacement”
intro.body: Been writing music since preteens, recently focused on AI music (since way before Suno — think OpenAI Jukebox). I view AI not as a replacement for my creativity, neither as a tool, but as a brilliant musician who can bring my ideas to life in ways I often wouldn’t have imagined. To be clear, I write most of my AI music starting from my own humming/piano playing/MIDIs, so it’s “mine” in most copyright senses.
